key_insight: Trial-level auditory oddball ERP waveforms, analyzed with deep learning, classified schizophrenia versus healthy controls better than models using conventional summary features.
clinical_relevance: This suggests EEG waveform-based machine learning may help develop objective, individual-level biomarkers for schizophrenia-related neural processing, though it is not yet a clinical diagnostic tool.
method: 258 patients with schizophrenia and 142 healthy controls were recorded during an auditory duration oddball EEG task.
EEG epochs were segmented from -100 to 500 ms and trial-level mismatch waveforms were created from deviant trials.
Five deep learning models on full residualized ERP waveforms were compared with classical models using 18 ERP summary features.
evidence_signal: On the held-out test set, deep learning achieved AUROC 0.797-0.857, outperforming classical feature-based models at 0.705-0.720.
watch_item: Results come from a single study design with fixed participant splits, so external validation and robustness across sites, devices, and populations are still needed.
paper_title: Deep Learning for Individual-Level Classification of Schizophrenia Versus Healthy Controls from Trial-Level Auditory Oddball ERP Waveforms
